title: isobuilder: build the pool index without apt-ftparchive
description: this got fixed in a less pure but less risky way just before release. seems the right point in the cycle to try a proper fix.
commit_message:
isobuilder: build the pool index without apt-ftparchive

apt-ftparchive assigns a deb to an architecture's index by globbing its
filename for "*_<arch>.deb", not by reading its control data, so on an
amd64v3 build every "*_amd64v3.deb" in the pool matched no index and was
silently dropped - leaving offline UEFI installs unable to find efibootmgr,
grub-efi-amd64, grub-efi-amd64-signed or grub-common (LP: #2169183).  Just
adding a binary-amd64v3 to its config is not enough: the glob then leaves
the plain "*_amd64.deb" packages in binary-amd64, which a variant-native
apt treats as supplanted and never reads.

`apt-cache show` already gives us the archive's index record for each
package, with Filename, Size and hash all correct, and we discarded all but
four fields of it.  Keep the record, put the deb at exactly the path its
Filename names, and the index is just those records written out and hashed.

Only binary-<variant> is generated on a variant build, as that is the only
index apt will read; the pool then needs an apt with
APT::Architecture-Variants set, which auto/build already configures.

--- a/debian/changelog
+++ b/debian/changelog
@@ -1,3 +1,16 @@
+livecd-rootfs (26.10.20) UNRELEASED; urgency=medium
+
+  * isobuilder: generate the ISO's Packages index directly rather than with
+    apt-ftparchive, which picks a deb's index by globbing its filename for
+    "*_<arch>.deb" and so silently dropped every "*_amd64v3.deb" from the
+    amd64v3 ISO, breaking offline UEFI installs (LP: #2169183).
+  * isobuilder: on a variant build generate only binary-<variant>, as a
+    variant-native apt treats binary-<base> as supplanted and never reads it.
+  * isobuilder: place pool debs at exactly their archive path, so the
+    archive's own index records describe the pool without rewriting.
+
+ -- Michael Hudson-Doyle <michael.hudson@canonical.com>  Mon, 05 Oct 2026 02:00:00 +0000
+

+        `apt-get download` picks its own name for the file and does not
